approach.method_basis: The Parent makes local graph edits from one scored current molecule, sanitizes and normalizes each identity, rejects duplicates and directly evaluates the first full batch allowed by inverse-motif memory. It moves to the highest-scoring accepted neighbor even after a worsening score and separately retains its best observation. Ring closure samples hydrogen-bearing attachment pairs within the existing graph-distance range and adds a bond; it can connect sites across already extensive ring frameworks. Same-transition bidirectional tabu matching, the repaired identity join and the established memory lifecycle remain in place.
approach.novelty: Add one topology gate specifically to new ring closures. A proposed closure may form a cycle whose chosen existing shortest path contains no old ring atom, one old ring atom, or two adjacent old ring atoms joined by an existing ring bond. These cases retain access to separate, spiro-like and single-edge fused additions while excluding more extensive overlap under this narrow rule. All edit sampling stays unchanged; an otherwise valid fresh rejected closure is replaced by continued sampling from the same source. This differs from the earlier sulfur filter, branch-removal menu and configuration assignment, and incorporates none of them.

observed_bottleneck: Parent n-9f7c7ec50039 completes the full panel at macro mean 0.5209178281192797 and standard deviation 0.004890242222897396, but its molecular assessment repeatedly identifies densely fused or bridged sulfur-rich rings with unresolved geometry. Its close_ring operator checks attachment hydrogens, graph distance and an inherited ring-size interval without restricting how the new cycle overlaps existing rings. An offline audit of all fifteen saved task logs finds 321 concrete closure draws, 318 valid novel closure candidates and 297 emitted closures. Under the exact path-overlap rule below, 258 of the valid novel candidates and 241 emitted closures have extended or separated overlap with existing ring atoms. This channel appears in every session. The remaining emitted closures comprise seven ring-disjoint paths, three one-ring-atom overlaps and 46 one-ring-edge overlaps. The restricted class is not uniformly unproductive: 37 of its emitted candidates beat their source, and 19 became the next current graph. These data establish an exercised topology channel and a real risk of sacrificing useful transitions, not that every excluded graph is strained. Sibling n-3dc00c8b2932 adds configuration labels but reports tied direct scores and persistent dense ring chemistry; n-93cd9a000278 improves sulfur valence yet retains problematic ring geometry. Neither sibling tests ring-closure overlap.
hypothesis: Reject an otherwise valid canonically novel close_ring neighbor before tabu testing unless its source shortest path overlaps the existing ring graph in zero atoms, one atom, or exactly one existing ring edge, thereby redirecting new-cycle proposals away from extended or separated ring overlap while retaining the Parent's edit sampling and accepted-score walk.

finding_summary.headline: Targeted ring closures disappear, while the mean score falls by 0.003396
finding_summary.insights:
The experiment establishes that a narrow source-path rule can strongly control ring-junction growth without disabling all closures or disturbing identity, memory and feedback. Most evaluated rings remain, and the admitted closure repertoire still produces improvements. The score cost is nevertheless real on this panel: the parent had 37 source-improving and 19 selected closures in the now-excluded class. Those historical observations explain why score retention required a test, but they do not provide scores for the newly rejected structures or identify which missing transition caused a later loss.

The chemical assessment shows what the topology restriction leaves unresolved. Less elaborate ring cages still contain unusual sulfur coordination, reactive heteroatom-halogen bonds and unspecified configurations. The permitted classes do not establish accessible three-dimensional geometry or synthetic plausibility, and the rule neither removes complexity already present in a source nor constrains other edit types. The campaign now has evidence that extensive ring overlap can be suppressed selectively, alongside evidence that this degree of suppression did not retain the registered mean-score margin. Ring topology and local chemical bonding remain separate limitations.
finding_summary.results:
The gate rejected 275 valid, fresh ring-closure attempts. Independent reconstruction of the current tabu table shows that 257 of these would otherwise have been admitted; each was replaced by a different neighbor from the same scored source before feedback. Emitted closures with extended or separated overlap fell from 241 to zero. Ring growth remained active through 40 permitted closures: six paths outside existing rings, three with a single old ring atom and 31 sharing one old ring edge. Nine permitted closures beat their source score and seven improved the best archive.

The overall molecules also lost much of the targeted complexity. Among 4,350 emitted neighbors, the number with a pair of RDKit-perceived rings sharing at least three atoms fell from 1,867 to 10, while mean ring-atom participation changed only from 62.89% to 61.70%. This preserved substantial ring content while removing most extensive ring overlap. All batches completed, requiring 12.83 attempts per ten submitted molecules versus 12.15 for the parent. The complete three-seed mean fell from 0.520918 to 0.517522, a paired change of -0.003396 that exceeds the allowed 0.002 loss. Seed changes were +0.004044, -0.024305 and +0.010073. DRD2 improved on average; the other four task means declined.

molecular.headline: Aromatic carbonyl and amine frameworks retain reactive halogens, unusual sulfur bonding and undefined stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: Every supplied current and parent trajectory was read. Each task has 900 recorded molecules and 870 optimizer proposals. The current output remains entirely ring-bearing by the digest's string counter, with aromatic-token rates from 0.9103 to 1.0 and mean SMILES lengths from 46.6 to 73.2. Molecules range from compact fused heterocycles to bulky aryl amines and expanded carbonyl-containing heterocycles. The leading structures generally have fewer elaborate cage connections than several parent families, but that does not make their bonding uniformly conventional. Ordinary thioethers, sulfoxides, amides and amines coexist with substituted S-H centres, multiply bonded sulfur carrying additional substituents, N-halogen groups, O-F groups and reactive sulfur-halogen connections. All charged-token and stereocentre-token rates are 0.0. Neutral SMILES do not establish neutral solution species for the amines, and the many potentially stereogenic ring and sulfur centres remain unspecified. Structural diversity is moderate across seeds and families, with the displayed leaders often concentrated in one closely related series. Synthetic plausibility and drug-likeness are limited primarily by unusual local bonding and reactive functionality, rather than by a lack of rings or heteroatoms.

per_task.generated_character: The leading seed-2 molecules are compact fused furan/unsaturated sulfur-ring systems bearing an aryl amide or pyridyl ketone. Alkyl, aminomethyl, imine and chlorinated amino substituents decorate the larger ring; the main ring sulfur itself is an ordinary divalent sulfide. The best molecule contains both an amino-chloromethyl substituent and an N-chloro amide. A close-scoring pyridyl-ketone relative has methylamino and imine groups without an N-halogen bond. Seed 1 retains a comparatively straightforward ethoxy/methyl/thiol indole carboxanilide. The low examples disrupt the attached aromatic ring, expand or open a heterocycle, or replace the compact carbonyl-containing connection with a more flexible heteroatom chain.
liabilities: N-chloro amides, N-chloro amines and amino-chloromethyl groups introduce reactive bonds beyond ordinary aryl chlorination.
Some alternatives contain labile imines, free thiols, sulfur-halogen groups or cumulated unsaturation.
Partly saturated fused rings and multiple unsaturated connections are not accompanied by defined stereochemistry or alkene geometry.
missing_features: The lowest ring-expanded and chain-like derivatives lack the intact aromatic carbonyl organization present in the stronger structures.

The high-scoring set lacks a systematic series that preserves the fused aromatic carbonyl framework while replacing reactive N-chloro and amino-chloromethyl groups with stable alternatives; a chlorine-free relative already shows that such chemistry can score closely.
Ring substituents with possible stereogenic relationships remain unassigned, and no configuration preference can be inferred from these strings.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The fused furan/sulfur-ring N-chloro amide scores 0.41700086027236194; a pyridyl-ketone relative with methylamino and imine substituents but no N-halogen group scores 0.4137456434408254. The ordinary indole carboxanilide reaches 0.39905049777278273. Thus the observed high-scoring family does not require every reactive chlorine substituent. A compact aryl-amide example scores 0.3957609793331631, while replacing its attached aromatic nitrogen-containing ring by an expanded unsaturated ring gives 0.01654726774958358. A pyridyl ketone at 0.40650757542526167 becomes 0.3305825215461728 when its carbonyl connection is replaced by a sulfoxide. The gradient favors retention of a compact aromatic carbonyl arrangement more clearly than sulfur enrichment. Current seed 2 reaches 0.41700086027236194 versus parental 0.41003927643747895 with a related but differently fused framework; seed 1 retains the same best indole amide, while seed 0 reaches 0.3504977161693128 versus 0.3966634883331815.

per_task.generated_character: The highest-scoring family is a bulky substituted phenyl group connected through an amino/exocyclic unsaturated arrangement to a nitrogen-containing carbonyl/imino ring. It carries branched conjugated carbon chains, fluoromethyl or difluoromethyl substituents, direct N-chlorination and an ester or imidate side chain ending in an aldehyde. Some side chains include an oxygen-linked alkyne, and some close relatives replace part of the carbon chain with additionally substituted, multiply bonded sulfur. The final seed-2 family instead contains an expanded nitrogen-rich dicarbonyl ring, imine and nitrile side chains, alkyl groups, methoxy groups and a bromoalkyl substituent. Early low examples retain more compact ester/phenol/dicarbonyl frameworks with disrupted ring connections. The assembled leading molecules have recognizable fragments but a high density of reactive or unusually conjugated connections.
liabilities: Direct N-Cl bonds, aldehydes and oxygen-linked alkynes introduce reactive functionality; the imidate alternative adds another hydrolysis-sensitive connection.
Extensive conjugated unsaturation and branching create configurational ambiguity and synthetic complexity.
Multiply bonded, additionally substituted sulfur and bromoalkyl groups appear in alternatives even where their local score advantage is not demonstrated.
missing_features: The low ring-altered compounds do not retain the same decorated aromatic and exocyclic heterocycle organization as the higher-scoring family.

Matched chemically simpler versions retaining that organization are underrepresented among the displayed leaders. Equal scores across several appendage changes do not demonstrate that the reactive or flexible embellishments are needed.
Imine and alkene geometry, and the configurations of branched side chains, are unspecified throughout the proposal set.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The leading imidate/alkyne/aldehyde derivative scores 0.6005008990495762, compared with 0.5976915588930607 for its carbonyl ester relative. Multiple variants share exactly 0.5976915588930607 despite changes in side-chain branching, alkene substitution, aminoalkyl substitution, aldehyde versus ketone termination, or introduction of an unusual sulfur-containing carbon-chain replacement. This supports the broader decorated aryl/heterocycle arrangement more strongly than those individual embellishments. Early ring-altered examples score 0.526081691583997 and 0.5266950153555399, while the initial aromatic dione scores 0.548381482770623. Relative to the parent, current seed 1 reaches 0.6005008990495762 versus 0.5906482326855353 with a different unsaturated decorated family. Current seed 0 and seed 2 reach 0.5925137762645043 and 0.5862876583994872 versus parental 0.6161710037174721 and 0.6092182584436399. The chemistry changes are mixed rather than a uniform preference for added complexity.

per_task.generated_character: The displayed leaders are bulky aryl-rich amines built around a saturated diaza ring with N-propyl and N-methyl substituents. A phenyl-pyridyl group and a chlorophenyl group provide aromatic surface, while a small saturated sulfur ring and an S-S connection link the latter to the amine framework. The small-ring S-H atom also carries an external sulfur substituent, giving an unusual neutral sulfur coordination state rather than an ordinary thietane. The diaza ring includes an aminal-like carbon connection. Other seeds produce amidine/amine-rich aryl compounds or more unsaturated sulfur rings. The low examples are carboxylic acid/amide/sulfonamide derivatives with much less freely basic aliphatic nitrogen. Familiar aryl and amine fragments are present, but the assembled sulfur-containing structures remain chemically questionable.
liabilities: The saturated S-H ring atom is additionally substituted, and the adjacent S-S connection adds chemical lability and synthetic uncertainty.
Aminal-like carbon connections, multiple basic nitrogen centres and extensive hydrophobic substitution occur together without a defined ionization state.
Alternative families add S-Cl, bromoalkyl, imine and unusually unsaturated sulfur functionality.
missing_features: The low acid/amide/sulfonamide molecules lack the accessible aliphatic amine organization found in the stronger aryl-rich products.
The displayed leaders lack a matched conventional-valence sulfur or carbon-linker series that preserves the useful saturated amine and aromatic arrangement.
The substituted diaza and sulfur rings have possible stereogenic relationships but no explicit assignments; the observed scores do not identify a preferred configuration.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The N-propyl diaza-ring molecule scores 0.9720943226453176. The corresponding N-ethyl relative scores 0.9310539197784231, while aromatic methyl, hydroxy or fluoro variants remain high but below the unmodified leader. This associates the observed scores with the aryl-rich saturated-amine arrangement and linker/substituent geometry. The early acid/amide/sulfonamide compounds score 0.007468397818197266 to 0.011875520467584314, so simply retaining nitrogen and aromatic rings is insufficient. Current seed 1 reaches 0.9720943226453176 versus the parent's 0.868020189804352, changing from a more fused unsaturated sulfur-containing framework to this diaza-ring family. Current seed 0 and seed 2 reach 0.8580723809662946 and 0.8946236316069243 versus parental 0.8856242185485628 and 0.9148143511682032. These cross-family observations do not establish a need for the unusual sulfur coordination.

per_task.generated_character: The leading family is a bulky expanded polyheterocycle with aromatic or pyridyl substituents, carbonyl groups, ether/ester-like connections, a cyclic sulfur-oxygen connection and an aryl alkyl sulfoxide. Nitrogen substituents include an N-S-H group or its N-S-Br relative. The main sulfoxide itself has a conventional bonding pattern. Other seeds contain cyclic imine/hydrazine/carbonyl frameworks or brominated aromatic compounds with acyl bromide and O-Br groups. Low-scoring examples open the carbonyl-containing ring, interrupt aromatic organization or introduce extended unsaturated chains. The products preserve much more ring and heteroatom content than simple fragments, but their large mixed N/O/S rings and reactive sulfur substituents make synthesis and stability uncertain.
liabilities: N-S-H, N-S-Br and cyclic S-O connections add reactive or labile chemistry within already complex rings.
Other seed families contain acyl bromide, O-Br and unusual substituted S-H groups.
Expanded mixed heteroatom rings increase conformational and synthetic complexity without a clear score benefit for several local extensions.
missing_features: The low ring-opened or extensively rearranged molecules fail to preserve the constrained aromatic/carbonyl organization of the stronger frameworks.

A matched series retaining that organization with ordinary stable ring connections and without terminal sulfur-halogen groups is incomplete. The N-S-H relative already scores above its N-S-Br partner, although N-S-H itself is not a general stability solution.
Possible sulfoxide and ring-centre stereochemistry is absent, and the large heterocyclic rings have no demonstrated preferred conformation.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The aryl-sulfoxide/polyheterocycle with N-S-H scores 0.20285512197228367, compared with 0.19999114123092163 for its N-S-Br relative. Extending a nearby ring connection in the brominated relative gives 0.20173664619648224. Extending the sulfoxide alkyl chain or adding a methylene before the pyridyl group gives 0.19905436822494996. These small differences support retention of the overall aryl/carbonyl/ring arrangement more clearly than a need for terminal sulfur bromination or further chain growth. Earlier ring-opened dicarbonyl derivatives score 0.12467972074136988 and 0.1263981386214515. Parent seed 2 reaches 0.20185639717998205 with a different expanded N/O/carbonyl framework, close to the current value. Current seed 0 and seed 1 reach 0.20020116392756776 and 0.18904611422707487 versus parental 0.2107445781802027 and 0.19092251395438758. The remaining shortfall cannot be assigned to a single absent functional group.

per_task.generated_character: The leading molecules contain compact nitrogen/carbonyl or imino heterocycles decorated with fluorinated carbon sites and unusually unsaturated sulfur rings. The best family includes a carbonyl/imino aza ring, an alkyl-fluorinated connection, a thiocarbonyl fluoride group and an O-F substituent attached through sulfur. Several sulfur centres are multiply bonded while carrying additional substituents, and others retain S-H within small rings. A second strong family has an NH-rich heteroaromatic dione with fluorinated small sulfur rings and a chlorinated side chain. These are less extensively caged than some parent leaders but remain synthetically questionable. Low molecules can already be sulfur-rich and ring-bearing, demonstrating that those features alone do not explain the score.
liabilities: O-F and thiocarbonyl fluoride groups are reactive functionality, not interchangeable with ordinary stable aryl or alkyl fluorination.
Small unsaturated sulfur rings contain unusual S-H and multiply bonded, additionally substituted sulfur centres.
Cumulated unsaturation has a string-level rate of 0.0828, and the wider trajectories include highly constrained sulfur-containing unsaturated rings; valid text does not establish feasible geometry.
missing_features: Low-scoring rearrangements fail to retain the compact heterocyclic carbonyl/imino and fluorinated-substituent arrangement present in the stronger families.

The displayed leaders lack a matched chemically stable series preserving that arrangement while replacing O-F, thiocarbonyl fluoride and unusually coordinated sulfur. The observed scores do not establish that these reactive bonds are required.
Potential stereogenic fluorinated carbon sites and ring junctions have no explicit configuration, and unsaturated small-ring geometries remain unresolved.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The leading fluorinated carbonyl/imino structure scores 0.6093265714673088; shortening its N-linked fluorinated side chain gives 0.5988225297176035. A related structure with carbon in place of an additional sulfur ring atom scores 0.5838393854264313 versus 0.5803523965017872 for the sulfur-containing partner, so sulfur enrichment is not consistently rewarded. In the second family, the heteroaromatic dione scores 0.533982380907913; a more saturated and reorganized carbonyl-ring variant scores 0.12049296847930738, while enlarging its small sulfur ring gives 0.41309444888784197. The observations favor particular polar-ring and fluorinated-substituent arrangements, not fluorine or sulfur counts alone. Current seed 0 and seed 2 reach 0.6093265714673088 and 0.533982380907913 versus parental 0.48118636011729826 and 0.4484554129767839 with denser sulfur cages. Current seed 1 reaches 0.35677909167534066 versus parental 0.5903526424693334, retaining highly unusual sulfur and unsaturation chemistry.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The cited leaders contain N-Cl, O-F, thiocarbonyl fluoride, N-S-Br and unusually substituted S-H atoms. Yet a chlorine-free aromatic carbonyl relative scores 0.4137456434408254, a conventional indole carboxanilide reaches 0.39905049777278273, and replacing terminal sulfur bromination by hydrogen changes a paired score from 0.19999114123092163 to 0.20285512197228367.
transferable_gaps.gap: Useful aryl, amine and carbonyl arrangements remain coupled to reactive halogen and sulfur chemistry.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Supply stable matched alternatives that retain useful fragment placement. Distinguish ordinary thioethers, thiols, sulfoxides and sulfones from unusual sulfur coordination, and distinguish conventional carbon-bound halogens from reactive heteroatom-halogen bonds.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Displayed low molecules often open a carbonyl ring, expand an attached aromatic ring or reorganize a compact aza-carbonyl framework. Such changes can produce scores of 0.01654726774958358 or 0.12049296847930738 even when much of the surrounding heteroatom and ring content remains.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve promising aromatic and polar-group organization when changing ring connectivity.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Generate matched changes in ring size, linker placement and heteroatom position that preserve useful local arrangements while exploring ordinary, geometrically feasible ring systems. Chemical diversity should include coherent alternatives to both ring opening and unusual sulfur-rich constructions.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Multiple decorated heterocycles share 0.5976915588930607 across chain branching, alkene substitution, terminal carbonyl changes and introduction of unusual sulfur. A carbon-containing ring relative scores 0.5838393854264313 versus 0.5803523965017872 for an additionally sulfur-substituted counterpart. Added complexity is therefore not consistently associated with higher scores in the supplied molecules.
transferable_gaps.gap: Chemically simpler relatives remain incomplete where several appendage changes have indistinguishable scores.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Include simplifications that reduce reactive bonds, excessive branching or flexible appendages while preserving the principal ring and functional-group arrangement. Let the existing score observations determine which chemically simpler structures retain useful behavior.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every task has stereocentre-token rate 0.0. The cited products contain substituted diaza rings, fluorinated carbon sites, sulfoxides, expanded mixed heteroatom rings and small unsaturated sulfur rings. Some families also show cumulated unsaturation, so chemically meaningful configuration extends beyond a single tetrahedral label.
transferable_gaps.gap: Stereogenic and highly unsaturated ring systems are emitted without explicit stereochemical identities or demonstrated geometric feasibility.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Represent feasible absolute and relative configurations and alkene geometry where applicable, preserve them through structural changes, and offer ordinary ring alternatives when a proposed topology demands severe geometric distortion. Do not infer synthetic accessibility from successful SMILES parsing alone.

method_name: Tabu search: de novo graph walks with expiring structural prohibitions
method_thesis: The anchor is the basic tabu-search procedure in Section 2 of [Glover, Tabu Search—Part I](https://leeds-faculty.colorado.edu/glover/TS%20-%20Part%20I-ORSA-aw.pdf), fixed before locating this external source. It chooses the best available admissible move, including a worsening move, while temporarily prohibiting reversals through short-term attribute memory. My molecular adaptation starts from the best supplied observation and maintains one current molecular graph, its true score, an independent best-observed archive, and expiring structural restrictions. At each feedback step, stochastically generate a new neighborhood through atom and bond edits, additions, deletions and chemically checked ring changes. Define move attributes from presence/absence changes of canonical local subgraphs around the edited region. After selecting a move, temporarily forbid a bounded record of its inverse attribute changes. These restrictions must apply to different canonical molecules sharing the affected local chemistry, so they can alter search beyond the protocol's mandatory whole-molecule duplicate rejection. Generate valid, canonical-unique, admissible neighbors until the announced batch is filled, then submit them directly without a learned score predictor. Only after real feedback choose the highest-scoring accepted neighbor as the next current graph, even when it scores below the current graph; retain the best score seen anywhere. Age restrictions by completed walk steps. If restrictions prevent sufficient fresh generation, release the oldest restrictions only as needed and record that release. This root uses the basic tabu form without an aspiration rule requiring unknown candidate scores. Preparation needs no learned model or corpus molecule store. Each objective restarts the same task-agnostic procedure with clean labeled and tabu state, and every proposed structure is generated online from the evolving current graph. The hypothesis is that an aggressive observed-neighbor choice combined with temporary structural reversal restrictions can move through useful intermediate structures and reach higher scoring molecular regions within the supplied feedback schedule. Activation requires restrictions to veto otherwise valid novel structural moves and thereby influence later current states. That diagnostic is insufficient by itself: success is the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. Overbroad attributes may suppress productive chemistry, while overly specific attributes may never affect novel proposals; the root must expose both possibilities.
